src/drivers/herdr.ts                  |  26 +++++--

✓ test: a slow-interface timing scenario completes deterministically by stepping the injected time source rather than sleeping (exit 0)
✓ test: the reconcile deadline scenario passes under an artificially slowed environment simulation (exit 0)
✓ test: no timing oracle in the touched suites sleeps against an uncontrolled real-time bound (exit 0)
✓ c1: The production changes are a pure mechanical substitution: three Date.now() call sites become this.time.now() and the two settle/poll sleeps become this.time.sleep with identical arguments (DELIVERY_SETTLE_POLL_MS, Math.min(DELIVERY_SETTLE_POLL_MS, remaining)). The constructor's new third parameter defaults to SYSTEM_TIME, whose now is Date.now and whose sleep is the exact former inline new Promise(setTimeout) expression, so with no injection every timing decision, constant, bound, and branch (readiness timeout arithmetic, reads>1 poll gating, remaining-budget clamp) evaluates identically to the pre-diff code. No production timeout constants changed (the 240_000→600_000 widening is test-file budget only), no error paths were reordered, and no completion-faking shortcut from the checklist applies — the seam is real dependency injection with a faithful system default, not an echo or stub.
